verdicts.explanation: The paper states Ag3SI has 3.8×10−2 S/cm '[15]' in Results 2.1, a literature citation, with no temperature given, so the origin, value, unit and null temperature are all correct.
The paper gives Ag7GeSe5I at 4.3×10−2 S/cm '[16]' in Results 2.1 and Table 2 lists it as σexp with ref [16]. It is a cited experimental value with no temperature, so the record is correct.
Results 2.1 gives Ag10Te4Br3 at 1.4×10−2 S/cm at room temperature '[17]', a cited value, and the record matches.

Results 2.1 gives Ag5Te2Cl at 1.0×10−1 S/cm at 341 K '[18]' and Table 2 shows the same @341K with ref [18]. The record is correctly literature_cited, and leaving the Celsius conversion null is acceptable.

Section 2.3 reports the FPMD-derived Li4InAs2F ionic conductivity of 8.0×10−2 S/cm (unit on the next line). The Methods state that the reported values are room-temperature conductivities, so computational origin and room temperature are supported. The unit_evidence_quote is not the value's own unit line, but the unit itself is correct.

Section 2.2 and Table 2 give Li6B7S13I a theoretical FPMD conductivity of 2.1×10−3 S/cm, listed under σ300K. Table 2 states room-temperature values, so null is conservative rather than wrong, and the material, value, unit and origin are correct.
